title: Birbal and the Gardener
summary: A poor palace gardener accidentally breaks Akbar's favorite china vase. Birbal helps the honest man turn an imperial death sentence into forgiveness.
full_text:
In the imperial palace of Agra, an elderly gardener named Ramdin had tended the roses, jasmine, and orange groves for forty faithful years. His devotion to the gardens was legendary, yet his hands were old and trembling.

One afternoon, while cleaning the marble pavilion, Ramdin accidentally brushed against a fragile, priceless porcelain vase gifted to Emperor Akbar by the Emperor of China. The vase crashed to the marble floor, shattering into a thousand irreparable pieces!

Hearing the crash, Akbar rushed into the room. Seeing his favorite heirloom destroyed, the Emperor flew into an uncontrollable rage:

'Careless wretch! That vase was irreplaceable! You have served me forty years, yet your clumsiness has destroyed a treasure of the empire! Guards, take this old fool to the dungeons! He shall be hanged tomorrow morning!'

Ramdin was dragged away, weeping bitterly.

When Birbal learned of the sentence, his heart ached for the faithful old gardener. He visited Ramdin in the dungeon and whispered a plan into his ear.

The next morning, Ramdin was brought before Akbar for his final execution. On a table beside the throne sat three other exquisite Chinese porcelain vases, identical to the one broken the previous day.

Akbar asked coldly: 'Old man, do you have any final words before you go to the gallows?'

Ramdin bowed respectfully: 'Sire, my life is forfeit. But since I am to die for breaking a vase, allow me to gaze upon these three remaining treasures and touch them with my hands one last time.'

Puzzled, Akbar permitted it.

Ramdin walked to the table, reached out his trembling hands, and with one swift, deliberate sweep of his arms, shoved all three remaining vases off the table, crashing them onto the marble floor where they shattered to pieces!

Akbar leaped from his throne, unsheathing his scimitar in fury: 'Madman! Are you insane? Why did you destroy the other three vases?'

Ramdin knelt calmly, folded his hands, and said with serene dignity:

'Your Majesty, you were about to execute me, an old man who served you faithfully for forty years, for accidentally breaking one vase. If these three remaining vases had stayed in the palace, three other innocent servants would eventually have broken them and been executed by your wrath!

'I have broken all three today so that I alone may bear the penalty, and three innocent lives may be saved from future execution!'

The entire court fell into dead silence. Akbar stood frozen, his sword lowering slowly to his side. The gardener's selfless sacrifice, orchestrated by Birbal's wisdom, shattered the Emperor's pride.

Tears of remorse filled Akbar's eyes. He sheathed his sword, embraced the old gardener, and said:

'Forgive me, Ramdin. Your compassion is a thousand times more precious than all the porcelain in China.' Akbar canceled the execution, granted Ramdin a lifelong pension, and thanked Birbal for saving him from cruelty.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Birbal and the Gardener"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
